meta.note: Mid-tail routine dispensing scaffold (Doc 29). Clinical numeric dosing ABSENT until founder review. Educational facts are original Materia authoring. Never copied from SAMF/MIMS/Lexicomp. AED enzyme induction, pregnancy/teratogenicity conversations, and migraine red flags are counselling hooks — Materia never invents a dose, level target, or taper. Benzodiazepines/amitriptyline live in mental-health — not duplicated here.

mechanism.value: Carbamazepine induces CYP enzymes and can reduce ethinylestradiol / hormonal contraceptive effectiveness — educational interaction flag only; confirm against current SA guidance.

action.value: Do not invent a dose change or backup schedule — escalate to the clinician for contraception counselling during enzyme-inducer AED therapy.

mechanism.value: Valproate inhibits lamotrigine's metabolism, roughly doubling its levels and significantly raising serious skin-reaction risk if titration isn't slowed accordingly.

action.value: Do not invent a dose change — this combination needs a specifically slower, guideline-directed titration schedule under clinical supervision.

mechanism.value: Isoniazid inhibits the hepatic enzymes that clear phenytoin, raising phenytoin levels toward toxicity in a drug with an already narrow therapeutic index.

action.value: Do not invent a dose change — flag for phenytoin level monitoring whenever both are co-prescribed, especially during TB treatment.

mechanism.value: Both drugs can independently slow heart rate — donepezil via cholinergic effects, atenolol via beta-blockade — so combined bradycardia risk is additive.

action.value: Do not invent a dose change — flag for pulse monitoring whenever both are co-prescribed, particularly in older patients.
